newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Endesa has solid H1 result before share offer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Endesa has solid H1 result before share offer.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Endesa posted a set of sound first-half results on Wednesday, setting the stage for what seems likely to be a successful public share offering in the autumn.
Endesa's attributable profit in the six months to end-June fell 3.9 percent to 78.59 billion pesetas, although cash flow grew by a healthy 46.2 percent to 233.75 billion.

The weakness in the bottom line was the result of heavy depreciation charges due to a change in the law last year which allows firms to restate the value of fixed assets in order to get tax benefits, which should begin to show next year.
Endesa said that without the effect of that asset restatement, net earnings would have risen 7.2 percent.
Furthermore, demand for electricity rose only slightly, up 1.4 percent in the period, and tariffs have been cut by three percent.
In view of all this, analysts' reception was positive.
"The figures show the firm's capacity to generate funds and its great profit potential, which is very positive ahead of the privatisation," said Alberto Nunez of BBV Interactivos brokerage.
State holding company Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales (Sepi) is to sell 25-35 percent of Endesa's capital in a mammoth public share offering in the autumn.
Given the prospect of a tide of fresh paper in what is a more difficult environment for the sector this year, Endesa has performed well, analysts said.

"If you take into account the fall in the tariff, the fact that demand is weak, the change in the regulatory environment and the asset restatement, its (share) performance has been outstanding this year," Nunez added.
"You've got to think that what (Sepi) is placing is no small amount," he added.
Endesa shares have climbed around 30 percent since December 30, and closed at 3,300 pesetas on Wednesday after the results got a warm welcome from the market.
One dealer at a foreign brokerage in Madrid said the results had outstripped his expectations, adding that future prospects are bright.
"There has been a one-off high depreciation charge, but the company will get that back in tax benefits in the next few years," he said.
But the forthcoming public offering is prompting caution.

Some believe that the upside potential for Endesa stock from now on is limited, despite the fact that 60 percent of the privatisation will be aimed at retail investors, practically guaranteeing that the offer will be taken up, they say.
"On a fundamental basis it's a very good company. I'd buy it long term, but neither is it a screaming buy at these levels," said a London analyst who requested anonymity.
He was more sceptical about the share offering and future company prospects.

"I think the privatisation will depend very much on how the market is in general. And no-one's expecting anything very spectacular from the company this year, or next for that matter. At the most we'll see five percent (profit) growth in 1998, but its more likely to be around three percent," he added.
